defineUNet3p

Source: R/segModels.R
defineUNet3p.Rd

Define a UNet3+ architecture for use in a luz training loop.

Usage

defineUNet3p(
  inChn = 3,
  nCls = 2,
  actFunc = "lrelu",
  encBlocks = "double",
  btnBlock = "double",
  skipProj = "conv3x3",
  useRes = FALSE,
  enChn = c(16, 32, 64, 128),
  outChn = 64,
  btnChn = 256,
  useASPP = FALSE,
  dilRates = c(6, 12, 18),
  dilChn = c(256, 256, 256, 256),
  negative_slope = 0.01,
  expRatio = 4,
  useDS = FALSE,
  stageLRs = NULL
)

Arguments

inChn

Number of channels, bands, or predictor variables in the input image or raster data. Default is 3.

nCls

Number of classes being differentiated. For a binary classification, this can be either 1 or 2. If 2, the problem is treated as a multiclass problem, and a multiclass loss metric should be used. Default is 3.

actFunc

Activation function to use throughout the non-ConvNeXt blocks. "relu" = ReLU; "lrelu" = leaky ReLU; "swish" = SiLU/Swish; "gelu" = GELU. Default is "lrelu".

encBlocks

Block implementation for the four encoder blocks. Either a single value applied to all four blocks or a length-4 character vector, with entries "double", "dws", or "convnext". Default is "double".

btnBlock

Block implementation for the bottleneck: "double", "dws", "convnext", or "aspp". Default is "double".

skipProj

Channel-unification convolution used on each branch of the full-scale skip connections: "conv3x3" (original UNet3+) or "conv1x1" (lighter). Default is "conv3x3".

useRes

TRUE or FALSE. Whether to include residual connections in the "double" and "dws" encoder blocks, the "double"/"dws"/"aspp" bottleneck, and the four per-node decoder feature-aggregation blocks (d1Blk-d4Blk). Has no effect on "convnext" blocks (always residual). Default is FALSE.

enChn

Vector of 4 integers defining the number of output feature maps for each of the four encoder blocks. Default is 16, 32, 64, and 128.

outChn

Number of channels each skip-connection branch is projected to before concatenation. Each decoder node therefore operates on 5 * outChn channels. Default is 64.

btnChn

Number of output feature maps from the bottleneck block. Default is 256.

useASPP

Deprecated. Use btnBlock = "aspp" instead. If TRUE and btnBlock is left at its default, the bottleneck is set to "aspp". Default is FALSE.

dilRates

Vector of 3 values specifying the dilation rates used in the ASPP module. Default is 6, 12, and 18.

dilChn

Vector of 4 values specifying the number of channels to produce at each dilation rate within the ASPP module. Default is 256 for each dilation rate.

negative_slope

Specifies the negative slope term for leaky ReLU activation. Default is 0.01.

expRatio

Inverted-bottleneck expansion ratio for "convnext" blocks. Default is 4.

useDS

TRUE or FALSE. Whether or not to use deep supervision. If TRUE, four predictions are made, one at each decoder block resolution, and the predictions are returned as a list object containing the 4 predictions. If FALSE, only the final prediction at the original resolution is returned. Default is FALSE or deep supervision is not implemented.

stageLRs

Optional numeric vector of length 9 specifying a base learning rate for each stage: encoder stages encoder1, encoder2, encoder3, encoder4 (including their cross-scale projections), the bottleneck (including its decoder projections), and decoder stages d1, d2, d3, d4 (in that order). Call model$get_param_groups() to obtain optimizer parameter groups. Default is NULL (single learning rate).

Value

UNet3+ model using nn_module().

Details

Define a UNet3+-like architecture with full-scale skip connections. The user can specify the number of output feature maps from each encoder block, the per-branch channel count used in the full-scale skip connections (outChn), and the bottleneck. Deep supervision can also be implemented. A variable number of input predictor variables and output classes can be defined.

As in the original UNet3+, downsampling within the full-scale skip connections uses non-overlapping max pooling and upsampling uses bilinear interpolation (there are no transpose convolutions). Each resampled branch is passed through a channel-unification convolution before the branches are concatenated; skipProj selects a 3x3 convolution ("conv3x3", the original UNet3+ design) or a lighter 1x1 convolution ("conv1x1"). The per-node feature aggregation block that follows each concatenation is always a 3x3 convolution.

Each of the four encoder blocks and the bottleneck can independently use one of three block implementations via encBlocks and btnBlock, matching defineUNet:

  • "double" - the standard double 3x3 convolution block (default). Becomes a residual double convolution block when useRes = TRUE.

  • "dws" - a double convolution block whose second 3x3 convolution is replaced with a depthwise separable convolution (dwsDoubleConv). Becomes a residual variant (dwsDoubleConvR) when useRes = TRUE.

  • "convnext" - a ConvNeXt-style block (doubleConvBlkCNX); always residual and always GELU, so useRes and actFunc do not affect these blocks.

btnBlock additionally accepts "aspp" for an atrous spatial pyramid pooling bottleneck, which also respects useRes (asppBlk vs. asppBlkR). The four per-node feature-aggregation blocks (d1Blk through d4Blk) likewise become residual when useRes = TRUE; since their input and output channel counts are always equal, the residual skip there is a parameter-free identity.

The architecture was inspired by:

Huang, H., Lin, L., Tong, R., Hu, H., Zhang, Q., Iwamoto, Y., Han, X., Chen, Y.W. and Wu, J., 2020, May. Unet 3+: A full-scale connected unet for medical image segmentation. In ICASSP 2020-2020 IEEE international conference on acoustics, speech and signal processing (ICASSP) (pp. 1055-1059). IEEE.
